idiom_name: EventEmitter listener (emitter.on) with a broker consume callback (amqplib channel.consume)
implementation_notes: Node's core is event-driven: listeners registered with emitter.on(name, fn) are called when the event fires, and every broker client adapts delivery to that model - amqplib's channel.consume(queue, onMessage, options) registers a callback the channel invokes per delivery, so the endpoint never calls receive(). This is native support: the classic endpoint object is replaced by a listener function plus its options, while the client's socket reader plays the caller. Only callback-style APIs expose this directly - when a client hands back an async iterator or a Readable stream, you are back in a pull loop and should treat it as the Polling Consumer.
pitfalls: noAck/autoAck=true acknowledges on receipt, before an async handler finishes - a crash mid-handler loses the message.
EventEmitter listeners run synchronously on the emitting thread: a slow or throwing listener blocks the event loop and can leave the consumer unacknowledged.
An unhandled 'error' event on a client emitter crashes the process; always attach an error listener to the connection and channel.
Every consume callback shares the single event loop, so CPU-bound handling must be offloaded or it stalls all other consumers.
